posts.title: Barracuda: Authorization Bypass (CVE-2026-116606) and Command injection (CVE-2026-111560)
posts.content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- An attacker with network access to an exposed administrative interface could fully compromise the appliance with root privileges, putting email, web, and application security infrastructure at risk.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS: 
For specific versions, please check the references
- **Affected by both vulnerabilities:**
 - Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG)    


- **Affected by the authenticated command injection only (CVE-2026-111560)**
 - Barracuda Load Balancer Application Delivery Controller (ADC)   
 - Barracuda Message Archiver (BMA)
 - Barracuda WAF Control Center (WCC)
 - Barracuda Web Application Firewall (WAF)
 - Barracuda Web Security Gateway (WSG)



##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:

- **Prerequisites:** Network access to the administrative interface of an affected device. Internet-exposed management interfaces carry the highest risk.
- **Impact Details:** The vendor advisory lists the authentication requirement as "administrative access," although it describes CVE-2026-116606 as a pre-authentication bypass.
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor patches are available. Many devices receive them automatically, If a patch has not been automatically applied, customers should manually apply the appropriate patch as soon as possible.
    - **Temporary:** Restrict administrative interfaces to trusted internal networks, apply network access controls, and re-enable automatic patching if it was disabled.

##### CVEs IN THIS ADVISORY:
- CVE-2026-116606 CVSS: 9.3 (CRITICAL) - Pre-authentication authorization bypass in ESG  
- CVE-2026-111560 CVSS: 8.6 (HIGH) - Command injection enabling root access across multiple products

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://trust.barracuda.com/security/pre-authentication-authorization-bypass-command-injection 
- Patch Information: https://documentation.campus.barracuda.com/wiki/x/n4BGOQ 


Supporting:
- News Coverage: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/barracuda-warns-of-critical-flaws-allowing-root-access-to-devices/ 

*Timestamp of the Information: 03.11.2026, 16:24*
posts.summary: Barracuda fixed a pre-authentication authorization bypass and a command injection flaw affecting several of its security and networking appliances. When chained together, they could allow an attacker with access to the administrative interface to bypass authorization controls and gain root access to the device.

posts.title: [Advisory] Progress WS_FTP Server: Critical authentication vulnerability ( CVE-2026-84295 )
posts.content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to steal administrative credentials over the network and potentially execute arbitrary commands, leading to full server compromise and data theft.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- Progress Software WS_FTP Server (Windows)
- affecting all versions prior to WS_FTP Server 2024.0.7 (9.0.7) and 2025.0.4.(10.0.4) both released 01.10.2026. 

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:
- **Attack Chain:** CVE-2026-84295 (improper authentication) exposes admin credentials to unauthenticated attackers. These could then enable command injection under certain configurations (CVE-2026-90868, CVE-2026-90865) or scope escape (CVE-2026-90863, CVE-2026-90866) leading to a complete compromise of the underlying server.
- **Prerequisites:** Network access to WS_FTP Server or its web interfaces. Several flaws require authenticated or delegated Host Administrator access, and some require specific configurations.
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor patches are available for both the 2024 and 2025 branches.   



##### CVEs RELATED TO THIS ADVISORY:
- CVE-2026-84295 CVSS3.1: 10.0 (CRITICAL) - Unauthenticated access to sensitive information, including admin credentials
- CVE-2026-90868 CVSS3.1: 9.9 (CRITICAL) - OS command injection enabling arbitrary command execution
- CVE-2026-90866 CVSS3.1: 9.1 (CRITICAL) - Path traversal by delegated Host Admin, potentially enabling RCE
- CVE-2026-90864 CVSS3.1: 9.1 (CRITICAL) - Path traversal allowing file access/modification outside scope
- CVE-2026-90863 CVSS3.1: 9.1 (CRITICAL) - Missing authorization in admin interface leading to privileged command execution
- CVE-2026-90865 CVSS3.1: 9.0 (CRITICAL) - OS command injection with elevated privileges


##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://community.progress.com/s/article/WS-FTP-Server-Critical-Security-Alert-Bulletin-September-2026 (Progress WS_FTP Security Alert Bulletin, Last Modified Date: 30.10.2026)

Supporting:

- Patch Information: https://docs.progress.com/bundle/wsftp-server-release-notes-2025/page/Whats-New-in-WS_FTP-Server-2025.html
- News Coverage: https://www.heise.de/en/news/Progress-WS-FTP-flaws-could-allow-system-compromise-11507793.html   

*Timestamp of the Information: 02.11.2026, 16:10*
posts.summary: Progress Software has disclosed numerous security vulnerabilities in its WS_FTP Server file transfer software for Windows, including a maximum-severity improper authentication vulnerability. This flaw lets unauthenticated remote attackers obtain sensitive information, including administrative credentials. Other vulnerabilities, including OS command injection, path traversal and missing authorization, can lead to arbitrary command execution and full compromise of the underlying server.

posts.title: [Advisory] Linux Kernel: Critical RCE via TCP Flaw (CVE-2026-98432)
posts.content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root via network access or intentionally crash the affected system.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- Linux Kernel
- Ubuntu
- Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL)
- Debian
- Amazon Linux
- SUSE / openSUSE
- Oracle Linux
For specific versions, please check the references.

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:
- **Prerequisites:** Network access to an exposed TCP service, with known exploits specifically targeting multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners.
- **Impact Details:** The use-after-free race condition in IPv4 TCP connections allows attackers to leak memory, bypass KASLR, and overwrite callback pointers. Vendor CVSS scores conflict based on differing attack complexity assessments.
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor patches available

##### CVEs IN THIS ADVISORY:
- CVE-2026-98432 CVSS3.1: 9.8 (CRITICAL) - Use-after-free race condition in TCP connection establishment leading to RCE

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:

*Timestamp of the Information: 29.10.2026, 19:15*
posts.summary: A critical security vulnerability has been identified in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP subsystem that could allow remote attackers to achieve root-level code execution or cause a denial of service. While an AI-generated proof-of-concept specifically targeted servers with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, it remains unconfirmed if systems without MPTCP enabled are similarly exploitable. Due to differing assessments of the attack complexity, major Linux distributions and the upstream kernel maintainers currently provide conflicting severity ratings for this flaw.

posts.title: VSCode: Trojanized Claude Code Extension Plants an SSH Backdoor
posts.content:
Phorion has discovered a compromise of the official Claude Code for VS Code extension on Open VSX, where the backdoored extension bundle contains a persistent Secure Shell (SSH) backdoor. Anthropic has removed the associated release the Open VSX extension, additionally pulling NPM and VSCode versions for 2.1.313 from their relevant registries.

We recommend you to:

1) Check if you use VSCode in your environment

2) Check if you have the compromised VSCode extension installed (Anthropic.claude-code version 2.1.313.)

3) Check for the relevant IOCs published in the blog posts referenced below

4) Use the script we have created to check a host for the relevant IOCs.

posts.title: [Advisory] Google Brotli: Critical OOB Write Enables RCE (CVE-2026-111497)
posts.content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code when an application decodes attacker-controlled Brotli data.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN, Proof of Concept Available

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- Google Brotli

**Impacted dependents & integrations:**
- Node.js
- Microsoft .NET, Visual Studio, PowerShell
- Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages
- Bun
- And many other third-party consumers

For specific versions, please check the references.

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:
- **Prerequisites:** Application decodes attacker-controlled Brotli data, such as compressed HTTP request/response bodies or compressed files; no authentication required.
- **Impact Details:** Out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder can corrupt adjacent memory, leak memory contents, crash the process, or enable arbitrary code execution.
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor patches available for affected products.
    - **Temporary:** Disable Brotli decoding of untrusted data and reject `Content-Encoding: br` until patched; restart services and rebuild containers after updating.

##### CVEs IN THIS ADVISORY:
- CVE-2026-111497 CVSS4.0: 9.2 (CRITICAL) - Out-of-Bounds Write in Google Brotli Decoder

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases
- Vendor Advisory: https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-111497

Supporting:

- Technical Analysis: https://www.imperva.com/blog/node2shell-from-brotli-data-to-remote-code-execution
- Technical Analysis: https://patchtheplanet.org/brotli
- Additional Sources: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35

posts.title: [Advisory] Cisco: Critical vulnerabilities affecting Expressway and Snort 3
posts.content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation could let unauthenticated remote attackers take full root-level control of Expressway devices, or compromise Snort 3-based security appliances, through network access.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- Cisco Expressway Series
- Cisco Open Source Snort 3 and Snort 3-based Cisco products
- Cisco Unified Communications products
- Cisco IOS XR Software
- Cisco Secure Client 

For specific versions, please check the references.

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:
- **Prerequisites:**
    - **Expressway:** The device is configured in a cluster. The attacker has network access to the database service and possesses the persistent cookies.
    - **Snort 3:** The attacker sends crafted network traffic that Snort 3 inspects. No authentication is required.
- **Impact Details:**
    - **Expressway:** Persistent cookies combine with missing client-certificate validation when TLS Verify Mode is enabled for clustering. This lets attackers invoke database RPC commands that execute as root.
    - **Snort 3:** Grouped memory-corruption and incorrect calculation flaws could compromise the inspection engine.
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor patches are available for all affected products. There are no workarounds for the Expressway, Snort 3, or Unified Communications issues.
    - Meraki MX, CDFW, and CSA instances were updated automatically by Cisco, so no customer action is required.

##### CVEs IN THIS ADVISORY:
- CVE-2026-76466 CVSS3.1: 9.8 (CRITICAL) - Expressway database service RCE as root via persistent cookies and missing certificate validation
- CVE-2026-76473 CVSS3.1: 9.8 (CRITICAL) - Unified Communications improper resource control (grouped CWE class)
- CVE-2026-76474 CVSS3.1: 9.8 (CRITICAL) - Unified Communications improper authentication, including bypass, session fixation, and replay (grouped)
- CVE-2026-76475 CVSS3.1: 9.3 (CRITICAL) - Unified Communications cross-site scripting / input neutralization flaws (grouped)
- CVE-2026-20043 CVSS3.1: 9.0 (CRITICAL) - Snort 3 out-of-bounds write issues (grouped)
- CVE-2026-20236 CVSS3.1: 9.0 (CRITICAL) - Snort 3 incorrect calculation issues (grouped). The vendor advisory lists 9.0, while the CVE record lists 7.5.


##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-notice-QGwHnJ6k (Cisco October 21, 2026 advisory bundle overview)

Supporting:
- News Coverage: https://www.securityweek.com/cisco-patches-34-vulnerabilities-across-multiple-products/ (SecurityWeek coverage of the patch release)

*Timestamp of the Information: 22.10.2026, 14:37*

posts.title: [Advisory] PHP2Shell: Critical Security Updates - Patch Now
posts.content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:

- Successful exploitation could allow remote attackers to execute code on affected servers, exposing application data and disrupting services.
- **Current exploitation status:** ~~UNKNOWN~~ **Update 21. October 12:35: Cloudflare claims first exploitation attempts.**
- **Public PoC claims:** Purported exploit code is publicly available, but its functionality and attribution to these vulnerabilities remain unverified.

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:

- PHP, maintained by the PHP Group.

PHP has not yet confirmed the affected versions. PHP 5.4 and later is claimed. For specific versions, please check the references.

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:

Individual technical causes and exploitation prerequisites remain pending official disclosure. No attack chain between the two vulnerabilities has been established publicly.

- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Security updates are scheduled for **21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC (16:00 CEST, Swiss time)**. PHP may release earlier.
    - Identify PHP-based applications, coordinate update readiness with hosting and software providers, and apply the official fixes promptly upon release.
    - **Temporary:** If prompt patching is not feasible, consider isolating internet-facing PHP applications from public networks.

##### CVEs IN THIS ADVISORY:

- CVE-2026-109618 CVSS4.0: 9.2 (CRITICAL) - Reported remote code execution. Individual technical details pending.
- CVE-2026-109619 CVSS4.0: 9.2 (CRITICAL) - Reported remote code execution. Individual technical details pending.


##### REFERENCES:

Primary:

- Source and Vendor Advisory: [PHP security team's advance release notice](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-20-1). Confirms severity and release schedule. Technical details and affected/fixed versions are pending.

Supporting:

- Additional Source: [CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-018](https://cert.europa.eu/publications/security-advisories/2026-018/). Public CVE identifiers, reported impact and interim isolation guidance.
- Additional Source: [watchTowr public FAQ](https://watchtowr.com/intelligence/php-cve-2026-109618-faq/). Exploitation-status reporting. Use PHP's notice for the current release schedule.
- Claimed Proof of Concept: [Third-party repository referencing php-up-2026](https://github.com/Zer061/CVE-2026-109618). Contains purported exploit code and detailed technical claims. Functionality and CVE attribution are unverified.
- Proof of Concept Video: [php2shell exploit demonstration](https://x.com/k_firsov/status/2112641845926989944), attributed to Calif. Demonstrates remote code execution against PHP. Claimed coverage of PHP 5.4 and later.


---
###### Update: 21. October 10:25

Additional public guidance is available covering PHP inventory, patch preparation and temporary measures to reduce exposure:

- Consider disabling session upload progress with `session.upload_progress.enabled = Off`.
- Evaluate blocking multipart requests at the web server or reverse proxy before they reach PHP, where application requirements permit.

**These measures are not confirmed to prevent exploitation of both vulnerabilities and do not replace patching. Blocking multipart requests can disrupt file uploads and forms.** Assess application compatibility and verify that restrictions are effective.

Source: [Vincent Schmalbach: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: What you should do now](https://www.vincentschmalbach.com/cve-2026-109618-and-cve-2026-109619-what-you-should-do-now/)

---
###### Update: 21. October 12:35

Cloudflare sees first explotation attempts

Source: [Dane Knecht CTO Cloudflare via X](https://x.com/dok2001/status/2112811965735202970)

---

###### Update: 21 October 2026, 15:45

#### PHP has released security updates for both vulnerabilities. Update immediately.

Official technical details and mitigation guidance are now available. The information below supersedes earlier preliminary statements in this post.

###### AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND FIXED VERSIONS:

All unpatched PHP installations serving web requests should be assessed, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed.

| PHP branch | Affected releases | Fixed release |
|---|---|---|
| 8.5 | Before 8.5.12 | **8.5.12** |
| 8.4 | Before 8.4.27 | **8.4.27** |
| 8.3 | Before 8.3.36 | **8.3.36** |
| 8.2 | Before 8.2.35 | **8.2.35** |

Older branches also require remediation. Distribution packages may contain backported fixes without changing the upstream version number. Verify the exact package against your provider's security advisory.

###### CONFIRMED VULNERABILITY DETAILS:

- **CVE-2026-109618, CVSS4.0: 9.2 (CRITICAL):** Out-of-memory handling can leave partially initialised request data in an invalid state. Processing this data during cleanup can lead to unauthenticated RCE.
- **CVE-2026-109619, CVSS4.0: 9.2 (CRITICAL):** Request-owned state can survive after its memory is freed. A subsequent request handled by the same worker can access that stale state, enabling RCE.

Successful exploitation executes code with the **web worker's privileges**.

PHP considers the risk highest for **Apache mod_php**, where exploitation has been demonstrated before application code executes. PHP-FPM is also affected: session-lifecycle RCE has been validated against both mod_php and FPM. Exploitability depends on the specific path, configuration and application.

###### REQUIRED ACTIONS:

- Update all affected PHP deployments, prioritising internet-facing applications and critical systems.
- Restart PHP workers and long-running PHP services after deployment. Verify that running instances use the patched build.
- For managed hosting and vendor appliances, obtain confirmation that the relevant fix has been deployed.
- For PHP 8.1 and older, check distribution or LTS-provider backports or migrate to a supported branch.
- PHP has exceptionally provided **minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1**. These do not restore regular upstream support.
- If timely patching is not possible, restrict access or temporarily isolate affected applications.

###### UPDATED TEMPORARY MITIGATION GUIDANCE:

**Only patching provides a complete solution. Configuration changes and WAF rules address individual paths and do not make an unpatched installation safe.**

- **Session paths:** Set `session.upload_progress.enabled=0` in startup configuration, such as `php.ini`, an FPM pool or server configuration, and restart every worker. **Do not rely on `ini_set()` or FPM `.user.ini`.**
- **PHP 8.5 fatal-backtrace path:** Set `fatal_error_backtraces=0` administratively and restart every worker. Other state-corruption paths remain possible.
- **OOM paths:** Assess administratively enforced `memory_limit=-1` alongside suitable container or cgroup memory boundaries. Underlying allocation failures remain possible. Do not substitute `RLIMIT_AS` or `RLIMIT_DATA`.
- Keep `post_max_size` conservative and enforce independent frontend limits on decoded request size, input fields, multipart parts, headers and nesting, including requests without a usable `Content-Length`.
- Block unnecessary multipart requests before they reach PHP. This can disrupt uploads and forms and does not cover every exploitation path.
- Remove invalid or deprecated per-request settings and address attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts. Suppressing error messages does not resolve these conditions.

###### SOURCES:

- [PHP official security announcement and remediation guidance](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php)
- [CVE-2026-109618: Official PHP advisory, RCE via OOM corruption](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w)
- [CVE-2026-109619: Official PHP advisory, RCE via stale global state](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp)
- [PHP release changelog](https://www.php.net/ChangeLog-8.php)

The linked security advisories contain detailed technical information.

---
###### Update: 21. October 16:25

Calif has published a detailed technical analysis of PHP2Shell, including exploit demonstrations and additional information on the affected execution paths.

**Source**: [Calif: PHP2Shell technical write-up.](https://calif.io/php2shell/) 

Contains detailed vulnerability analysis and exploit demonstrations.

---
###### Update: 21. October 16:38

**Practical patching guide and additional technical analysis available**

Mattias Geniar has published a practical guide covering PHP updates on Debian, Ubuntu and RHEL-based systems, container deployments, required service restarts and verification that patched PHP is actually running.

Wiz Research has also published a detailed technical write-up. In addition to remote code execution, Wiz demonstrates unauthenticated disclosure of PHP process memory, potentially exposing passwords, authentication tokens and API keys without executing code on the server.

**Source:** 
- [Mattias Geniar: How to apply the patches](https://ma.ttias.be/php-cve-2026-109618-patch/)
- [Wiz Research: PHP2Shell technical analysis and impact](https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce)
---

###### Update: 21. October 16:50

**PHP2Shell** is now used as the collective name for the vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. We have updated this post’s title accordingly.

The researchers’ dedicated website brings together vulnerability information, patching guidance and links to technical analyses.

**Source:** [PHP2Shell: Official vulnerability website](https://www.php2shell.com/)

---

###### Update: 21. October 19:35

**Further unverified vulnerability reports**

Additional PHP vulnerability claims are circulating, including reports concerning recently patched versions. These may involve separate issues and do not, by themselves, establish a bypass of the PHP2Shell fixes.

Apply the available patches without delay. Continue monitoring official PHP and vendor advisories, and remain prepared to deploy further security updates or hotfixes. Further research may uncover additional vulnerabilities or exploitation paths.

We will not publish an update for every unverified claim. We will update this post when confirmed, relevant findings change the risk assessment or recommended actions.

---
###### Update: 22. October 02:10

**Threat-hunting and detection resources**

Additional resources are available to support investigation of suspicious activity on PHP-based systems:

- [Zeek and Suricata](https://github.com/corelight/php2shell-detect): Network detection rules published by Corelight.
- [Elastic](https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/threat-command/php2shell-php-rce-detection): Behaviour-based detection guidance and rules for suspicious web-server activity.
- [Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel](https://github.com/cseelhoff-ms/php2shell-hunting-pack#table-2-hunt-for-exploitation): Third-party hunting queries covering process activity, crashes, file creation and network connections.

Coverage depends on available telemetry and local configuration. Rules and queries require validation and tuning. Findings do not independently confirm exploitation of these vulnerabilities, and an absence of findings does not exclude compromise.

These resources complement patching and incident investigation.

---
posts.summary: PHP has announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities. Public reporting associates these issues with unauthenticated remote code execution. Organisations should identify PHP deployments now and prepare to update promptly when fixes become available.
